movie.title: Horsegirls
movie.overview: As her mother battles an uncertain diagnosis, neurodivergent 22-year-old Margarita discovers a source of strength in an unexpected place: the sport of hobbyhorsing.

reviews.author: The Fixate & Binge Podcast, w/ Joe Curdy
reviews.content:
Writer and director Lauren Meyering's feature film debut, **HORSEGIRLS**, may seem to follow a familiar pattern for films of this genre, but the performances from its very talented cast are what ultimately set it apart.

Meyering's film, inspired by co-writer and co-producer Mackenzie Breeden's own experiences, introduces us to Margarita (Lilian Carrier), a 22-year-old autistic woman living with her mother Sandy (Gretchen Mol) in a small town in Oregon.

We learn that Margarita is passionate about horses, riding around town on "Cheeseburger," a modified tricycle that resembles a horse, as she struggles with the idea of growing up. However, as Sandy's third round of chemotherapy for cancer comes to an end with diminishing returns, the fiercely protective mother is compelled to push Margarita out of her comfort zone and toward accepting more adult responsibilities.

Amid the anxiety and stress of so much change -- the kind of upheaval that can pose additional challenges and uncertainty for neurodivergent individuals -- Margarita stumbles upon a local club of competitive Hobby Horse riders, led by Coach (Jerod Haynes). Enthralled, she joins the group, and despite the social awkwardness of competing alongside much younger riders, Margarita is seen for the first time in a larger social setting as happy, inspired, and driven.

Nevertheless, these whimsical activities are precisely the things her mother Sandy has discouraged. When Sandy discovers the Hobby Horse club, it creates a rift in their mother/daughter relationship at the worst possible time.

Co-starring Tony Hale and Iqbal Theba (both of whom feel somewhat underwritten here), **HORSEGIRLS** still astonishes with sincere writing that never drifts into mawkishness. But it is the incredible performances of Mol and Carrier that truly capture the heart of the film.

As a neurodivergent actress herself, Carrier's performance brings a level of weight and authenticity that surprises and charms throughout. Mol's depiction of Sandy -- a loving but protective mother facing an uncertain future -- is heartbreaking, triumphant, and sincere; arguably a career-best performance.

**HORSEGIRLS** inspires and embraces viewers in all the right places.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Facing the uncertainty of her mother's mysterious illness, neurodivergent 22-year-old Margarita finds solace, confidence, and community through the unconventional world of hobbyhorsing.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Margarita, a neurodivergent young woman navigating the complexities of early adulthood, finds her life upended when her mother receives an uncertain medical diagnosis. Stressed and seeking an outlet, she unexpectedly discovers the passionate world of hobbyhorsing. Through this unique sport, Margarita finds a powerful creative escape and a comforting sense of control amid familial hardship. Ultimately, the hobby empowers her to build resilience, embrace her identity, and confront her fears with renewed optimism.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Margarita is a 22-year-old neurodivergent woman whose routine is shattered when her mother falls ill with an elusive, ambiguous medical condition. As family dynamics strain under the weight of diagnostic uncertainty, Margarita struggles to process her anxiety and find emotional stability. Seeking a distraction, she stumbles upon a local community dedicated to hobbyhorsing—a sport combining athletic jump courses with handcrafted wooden horse heads. Initial hesitation quickly gives way to fascination as Margarita immerses herself in the discipline, creativity, and physical exertion required by the passion. The structured nature of the hobby offers her a safe haven where her neurodivergent traits are embraced rather than misunderstood. Along the way, she connects with fellow enthusiasts who teach her that strength often springs from unexpected places. Balancing her responsibilities at home with her newfound dedication, Margarita learns to use the sport's emotional leverage to support her mother. As her mother's medical journey unfolds, Margarita stands tall on the competition course, demonstrating how creative self-expression can transform vulnerability into genuine resilience.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Horsegirls is a heartwarming comedy-drama that explores the healing power of niche subcultures, neurodivergent self-discovery, and unconditional family bonds. When 22-year-old Margarita faces the emotional turmoil of her mother's lingering medical uncertainty, she unexpectedly discovers hobbyhorsing. What begins as an unusual distraction quickly turns into a transformative journey of empowerment, community, and personal growth, offering a unique look at coping with life's unpredictable hurdles through creativity and play.

story_structure.resolution: Through her journey in the sport, Margarita finds resilience and identity, emerging with a renewed sense of strength and self-acceptance as she and her family navigate the future together.
story_structure.introduction: Neurodivergent 22-year-old Margarita navigates the emotional strain of her mother's mysterious, worsening illness while searching for a sense of control and belonging in her daily life.
story_structure.risingAction: As Margarita immerses herself in training and local competitions, she builds meaningful connections with fellow participants, constantly balancing her growing devotion to the sport with her caretaking responsibilities at home.
